cards.title: Noticing is the turning point
cards.teaching_point: Realising that attention has wandered is already a moment of awareness.
cards.explanation: The aim is not to stop wandering. The useful moment is noticing where attention went, then choosing to begin again without blame.
cards.daily_life_application: Use one moment of noticing before returning to an ordinary task today.

cards.title: An anchor is not a grip
cards.teaching_point: An anchor gives attention somewhere to return without asking you to hold it there by force.
cards.explanation: Attention can rest lightly on one clear sensation. When it moves away, the practice is to return rather than tighten or strain.
cards.daily_life_application: Choose one simple sensation as an anchor during a busy moment.

cards.title: Enough effort, without strain
cards.teaching_point: Meditation needs enough effort to remember the practice, with enough ease to keep returning.
cards.explanation: Too little effort becomes drifting. Too much becomes strain. A workable middle is alert, gentle, and willing to begin again.
cards.daily_life_application: Notice once today whether a task needs more attention or less strain.

cards.title: Sensation before the story
cards.teaching_point: Direct sensation and the mind's description of it are two different parts of experience.
cards.explanation: You can first notice pressure, warmth, movement, or sound. The names and opinions that follow can be noticed without becoming the anchor.
cards.daily_life_application: Pause once today to notice a direct sensation before naming or judging it.

cards.title: Attention can narrow and widen
cards.teaching_point: Attention can rest on one detail and later widen to include the larger field around it.
cards.explanation: A narrow focus makes the anchor clear. A wider focus can include body, sound, and space while the anchor remains available for returning.
cards.daily_life_application: Move from one detail to the wider room during one ordinary pause.

cards.title: A thought is an event
cards.teaching_point: A thought can be noticed as something happening now, rather than an instruction that must be followed.
cards.explanation: There is no need to remove the thought. Notice that thinking is present, then choose whether to return to the practice.
cards.daily_life_application: Notice one thought today before deciding whether it needs your attention.

cards.title: Kindness is an intention
cards.teaching_point: Kindness practice offers a direction of goodwill without demanding a particular feeling.
cards.explanation: The phrase can be repeated sincerely even when warmth does not appear. The practice is the willingness to offer it, not a mood to produce.
cards.daily_life_application: Offer one quiet wish of goodwill during an ordinary meeting today.

cards.title: Rest is not a test
cards.teaching_point: A rest practice does not need to force sleep or prove that you are relaxing correctly.
cards.explanation: The task is only to reduce effort and return to a simple resting anchor. Sleep may come, while quiet rest remains enough for the practice.
cards.daily_life_application: Let one short pause today be rest rather than another task to complete.
